title: Antithrombotic strategy after TAVI by atrial fibrillation status and CT leaflet thrombosis: reconstructed-IPD network meta-analysis with a pre-specified update at the next trial readouts

pico.population: Adults after successful TAVI, stratified by AF or other OAC indication versus none
pico.intervention: Single antiplatelet therapy, DOAC, vitamin K antagonist, or CT-guided therapy
pico.comparator: Each other strategy, including dual antiplatelet therapy
pico.outcomes: All-cause death, stroke or thromboembolism, major bleeding, net clinical outcome, CT-defined leaflet thrombosis
pico.timing: Time-to-event from TAVI to 1 year, with landmark analyses at 30 days

decision: Which antithrombotic regimen to prescribe at discharge after TAVI, and whether CT-detected leaflet thrombosis should alter it.
decision_maker: Interventional and structural cardiologists, heart teams, guideline committees
why_now: Trials in the appraised subset point in different directions (rivaroxaban inferior to antiplatelet therapy in 31733180, edoxaban and apixaban not superior to standard care or vitamin K antagonist in 34449183 and 35583186, bleeding excess with added clopidogrel in 32223116 and 32865376), while several adequately sized trials are registered to report from 2027. The latest meta-analysis in the subset (29516608) predates all of them. Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

competing.note: Ticagrelor or aspirin as single antiplatelet therapy after TAVI; a single comparison within the network
CT-guided personalised therapy versus lifelong single antiplatelet therapy, non-AF patients
Anticoagulation versus aspirin; registry shows COMPLETED

designs.primary: Reconstructed-IPD network meta-analysis, random-effects with REML and Hartung-Knapp adjustment, landmark and restricted mean survival analyses, registered on PROSPERO with an update pre-specified for each listed readout
designs.alternative: Registry-based randomised trial of antiplatelet de-escalation within a national TAVI registry

data_required: Published Kaplan-Meier curves and event tables from all randomised antithrombotic trials after TAVI; aggregate leaflet thrombosis CT data
feasibility: High: within the owner's reconstructed-IPD and NMA methods; no data access needed. Fewer than ten eligible trials until 2028.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects. Cross-domain overlap with D8 candidate questions on antithrombotic therapy after TAVI; merge at consolidation.

G1.note: Prescribing after TAVI is a near-universal decision judged on death, stroke and major bleeding.

G2.note: Trials conflict on DOAC and antiplatelet strategies (31733180 versus 34449183 and 35583186). Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No trial in the file covers the full network; the nearest, NCT05283356 (N=1206, 2027-06), compares two single agents. The only meta-analysis in the subset (29516608) is from 2018 and pooled 840 patients; trials published since (31733180, 32865376, 32223116, 34449183, 35583186) add 1644+665+313+1426+1500 = 5548 randomised patients. Meta-analyses outside the appraised subset were not searched.

G4.note: A network analysis with reconstructed time-to-event data would be citable by a guideline committee where pairwise pooling cannot compare DOAC with antiplatelet therapy across AF strata.

G5.note: Not a repeat of the same trials: the evidence base has grown roughly sevenfold since the last pooled analysis and the pre-specified update design addresses the 2027 to 2028 readouts.

impact.why: TAVI is performed in very large numbers and every patient needs a discharge antithrombotic decision.

novelty.why: Pairwise meta-analyses exist; the network structure, AF stratification and leaflet thrombosis linkage are new.

equipoise.why: Trials in the subset conflict on DOAC versus antiplatelet therapy and on dual therapy.

design.why: Reconstructed-IPD network meta-analysis with pre-specified updates is credible but limited by open-label trials.

timeliness.why: Six registered trials report between 2026 and 2028.

citation.why: Antithrombotic meta-analyses in target-tier journals are well cited but crowded.

feasibility.why: Entirely within the owner's methods with public data.

next_actions: Register the protocol on PROSPERO with the readout-triggered update rule
Extract Kaplan-Meier curves and event counts from the nine key trials and build the reconstruction pipeline
Check D8 candidates for duplication and agree a single owner of the question

status_history.reason: Proposed from appraised D3 subset; gates G1 to G5 passed on trial evidence

title: Cardiometabolic and neurohormonal drugs after TAVI: target trial emulation benchmarked against the DapaTAVI randomised result

pico.population: Adults discharged alive after TAVI for severe aortic stenosis, without prior use of the study drug
pico.intervention: Initiation of an SGLT2 inhibitor, a GLP-1 receptor agonist or a renin-angiotensin inhibitor within 90 days
pico.outcomes: All-cause death or heart failure hospitalisation; major adverse cardiovascular events; kidney outcomes
pico.timing: Time zero at the end of the grace period after discharge; follow-up to 3 years

decision: Whether to start SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists or renin-angiotensin inhibitors routinely after TAVI, and in whom (frailty, diabetes, ejection fraction).
decision_maker: Structural and heart failure cardiologists; guideline committees
why_now: A single open-label trial (40162639) reported fewer events with dapagliflozin, a post hoc analysis suggests the effect lies in frail patients (42885795), and observational data suggest benefit of GLP-1 receptor agonists and renin-angiotensin inhibitors (42886864, 30512100, 31370954) with no randomised test of those classes yet reported. Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

competing.note: Enavogliflozin after TAVR; 26 months from the date of this landscape
Finerenone after TAVI with heart failure

designs.primary: Sequential target trial emulation with clone-censor-weight handling of grace periods, with the DapaTAVI estimate (40162639) used as a negative and positive control for the identification strategy
designs.alternative: Registry-based randomised trial of renin-angiotensin inhibitor continuation versus withdrawal after TAVI

data_required: National TAVI registry linked to dispensed prescriptions, hospital episodes and mortality, with frailty and echocardiographic variables
data_sources: National TAVI registry with prescribing linkage (access not yet established)
UK Biobank QMUL extract (few TAVI recipients expected; not checked)
feasibility: Medium: the method is within the owner's skills and prior UK Biobank work on SGLT2 and ACE inhibitors in aortic stenosis, but a linked registry with prescribing data needs collaborators.
overlap: None with active projects; methodological proximity to the owner's UK Biobank work in aortic stenosis.
target_journal: JAMA Cardiology or European Heart Journal

G1.note: Heart failure hospitalisation and death after TAVI are the endpoints that define the prescribing decision.

G2.note: Only one randomised trial (40162639) exists and it tested one drug; observational signals for other classes are untested. Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: The nearest adequately powered trial, NCT05672836 (N=1040), reports 2028-12, beyond 24 months; the other registered trials are 2029 to 2030 or small. This margin is narrow and should be rechecked monthly.

G4.note: Benchmarking against the randomised estimate gives a credible validation of the emulation, which a committee could weigh alongside the trials.

G5.note: Not a repeat meta-analysis; the largest existing pooled report (42919410) is dominated by observational studies and one trial.

impact.why: Several hundred thousand TAVI recipients with high rates of heart failure hospitalisation, and drugs that are cheap and widely available.

novelty.why: No emulation benchmarked to the randomised trial; GLP-1 receptor agonists and renin-angiotensin inhibitors untested by trial.

equipoise.why: One positive open-label trial favours SGLT2 inhibitors; other classes remain uncertain.

design.why: Emulation is credible with a benchmark, but confounding by frailty and indication remains.

timeliness.why: Readouts begin in late 2028; the window to inform trial design is now.

citation.why: Post-TAVI drug therapy follows a high-citation NEJM trial and sits at the intersection of structural and heart failure care.

feasibility.why: Needs a linked national dataset not yet secured.

next_actions: Identify a national TAVI registry with prescribing linkage and open collaboration
Write the target trial protocol with the DapaTAVI emulation as the first analysis
Quantify TAVI recipients in the UK Biobank extract to decide whether it can contribute

status_history.reason: Proposed from appraised D3 subset; gates G1 to G5 passed on trial evidence

title: Lifetime management of severe aortic stenosis in younger and low-risk patients: decision model with value-of-information analysis including redo strategies

pico.population: Patients with severe aortic stenosis who are low surgical risk, by age band
pico.intervention: TAVI-first lifetime strategy (including TAV-in-TAV or explant at failure)
pico.comparator: SAVR-first lifetime strategy (including valve-in-valve at failure)
pico.outcomes: Quality-adjusted life years, lifetime cost, death, stroke, reintervention

decision: Which first valve strategy to recommend for patients under about 75 years, and whether further trial evidence is worth its cost.
decision_maker: Heart teams, guideline committees, funders such as NIHR
why_now: Long-term trial results diverge: 10-year all-cause mortality was 86.1% after TAVR versus 82.8% after surgery in intermediate-risk patients (42300821, HR 1.13; 95% CI 1.02-1.25), whereas NOTION showed 65.5% in both arms at 10 years (38321820) and low-risk trials show no significant difference to 7 years (41144631). Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

competing.note: START YOUNG; surgical versus transcatheter in young patients; primary outcome not recorded in the trials file
AMETHYST; isolated SAVR in low-risk patients
REPEAT; repeat intervention for failed surgical bioprostheses

designs.primary: Patient-level Markov microsimulation with probabilistic sensitivity analysis and expected value of perfect and partial perfect information, parameterised from trial time-to-event data and redo registries
designs.alternative: Reconstructed-IPD analysis of restricted mean survival time across all TAVI versus SAVR trials by age

data_required: Reconstructed time-to-event data from low- and intermediate-risk trials; redo-TAVR and reintervention rates; UK or European cost and utility inputs
feasibility: High: matches the owner's Markov microsimulation and reconstruction skills.
overlap: Method overlap only with the owner's Markov microsimulation of Impella in STEMI-related cardiogenic shock; no topic overlap.

G1.note: First-valve choice in younger patients is a common decision with lifetime consequences.

G2.note: Long-term mortality results conflict between PARTNER 2A and NOTION-type results. Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: START YOUNG (NCT06861361, N=1180, 2028-09) and DEDICATE (NCT03112980, N=1414, 2028-01) are registered to complete within 24 months; whether either is adequately powered for lifetime outcomes cannot be judged because the trials file records no primary outcome. A target-tier meta-analysis (40044297, 2025-03-11) also falls inside the 24-month window; since then new follow-up (42300821, 41144631, 41697183) has accrued but the change in pooled events is not quantified from the stored abstracts.

G4.note: A value-of-information analysis would state which parameter justifies a further trial and its size, which funders can use even if a trial reports first.

G5.note: A decision model with VOI is not a repeat meta-analysis; the reconstructed-IPD component is secondary.

impact.why: Age-expanding indication affects the largest group of TAVI candidates with decades of follow-up.

novelty.why: Lifetime models exist in the literature for individual trials; VOI with redo strategies is less developed (not verified outside the subset).

equipoise.why: Trials diverge at 10 years in intermediate-risk and are neutral in low-risk patients.

design.why: Credible but dependent on extrapolation and thin redo data.

timeliness.why: Two trials complete within 24 months; value falls if the model appears after them.

citation.why: Lifetime strategy questions in aortic stenosis attract high attention in target journals.

feasibility.why: Within owner's skills; costs and utilities need sourcing.

next_actions: Quantify new pooled events since 40044297 to resolve the G3 uncertainty
Retrieve the primary outcomes of NCT06861361 and NCT03112980 from the registry
Draft the model structure with redo pathways and a VOI plan

status_history.reason: Proposed from appraised D3 subset; G3 fails on registered trials and requires resolution before promotion

title: Management of severe aortic stenosis presenting with cardiogenic shock: TAVI, balloon valvuloplasty or medical therapy, with or without mechanical circulatory support

pico.population: Adults admitted with severe aortic stenosis and cardiogenic shock
pico.intervention: Early TAVI, or balloon aortic valvuloplasty as a bridge, with or without temporary mechanical circulatory support
pico.comparator: Medical therapy or delayed valve intervention
pico.outcomes: In-hospital and 1-year mortality, renal replacement therapy, stroke, length of stay

decision: Whether and how fast to offer valve intervention, and with which support, to patients in shock who were excluded from the pivotal TAVI trials.
why_now: The one large registry analysis in the subset (37350747; 5006 of 309 505 TAVR patients presented in shock) shows higher mortality in patients presenting in shock than in matched patients without shock (in-hospital 9.9% vs. 2.7%), but cannot compare against non-intervention. No randomised trial appears in the trials file. Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

designs.primary: Target trial emulation in linked national hospital data and shock registries, comparing early TAVI, valvuloplasty and medical therapy with time zero at shock recognition
designs.alternative: Prospective multicentre registry with embedded randomisation of timing

data_required: Linked admissions with aortic stenosis and shock codes, procedure dates, mechanical support and mortality, with haemodynamic severity
data_sources: BCIS and ICNARC registries through collaborators (aortic stenosis coverage not confirmed)
feasibility: Low to medium: the owner has shock registry access, but whether those registries record aortic stenosis aetiology and non-TAVI comparators is unknown.
overlap: Adjacent to the owner's review of acute mitral regurgitation and cardiogenic shock and the shock organisation SRMA; no duplication of either.

G1.note: A high-mortality setting where the decision is whether to intervene at all.

G2.note: No randomised evidence is in the stored records and the only registry study cannot compare with non-intervention. Guideline position unverified (guideline extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only.

G3.note: No registered trial is in the trials file; the search of the file was by keyword for shock and may miss differently worded entries.

G4.note: No dataset with both an intervention and a non-intervention arm, valve severity and shock severity has been identified; immortal-time and selection bias would be severe, so a weaker design would not be citable. Unresolved until a dataset is confirmed.

G5.note: Not incremental if a comparator is available; the existing analysis (37350747) is a single registry of TAVR recipients only.

impact.why: Rare presentation but very high mortality.

novelty.why: Only one registry description of TAVR in shock appears in the stored subset.

equipoise.why: No randomised evidence and no stored comparison with non-intervention.

design.why: No identified dataset supports a credible comparison.

citation.why: The previous analysis appeared in the European Heart Journal; the niche is small.

feasibility.why: Access to a suitable dataset is unconfirmed.

next_actions: Check whether BCIS and ICNARC registries capture aortic stenosis as shock aetiology
Search for hospital administrative datasets with valve and shock codes
Decide at the next review whether to park the question under G4

status_history.reason: Proposed from appraised D3 subset; G4 fails pending dataset identification
